analysis:
Examined the visible head text of ClusterService.swift (lines 911-1577) and the ClusterServiceControl.swift patch. The supplied ClusterService.swift text is mostly unchanged surrounding code (checkForUpdate, checkApproval, supervise, stopChild, publish). The changed portions (init `listening`, `listenerChange`, responder visibility, 337-420 head ranges) fall outside the supplied excerpts, so I could not review them.

The ClusterServiceControl.swift changes are security-relevant but narrow. First, ensureControlResponder now recreates the control listener when `listenerChange` reports a cable-port move or a new pairing, so a listener keyed to an old pairing is torn down. Second, it takes its selection from `listenerSelection()` instead of `context.linkSelection()`, and its port and policy from an injected `listening` object instead of the fixed `ClusterSetupLinkExchange.controlPort`. Third, ensureControl now also drops the control node when `node.localID` differs from `pairing.localMemberID`, which closes a stale-identity case after the Mac re-pairs under a new key. That tightens pairing binding.

Nothing visible regresses a TB-011/T-053 binding, and no changed code reaches inference traffic, provider attestation or the prefix cache (T-041, which was supplied as relevant but is not touched here).

Unverified contracts the next pass should check:
(1) The definitions of `Listening` (default port and policy), `listenerSelection()` and `listenerChange`, to confirm the production default keeps `controlPort` and the same policy, and that a non-default `listening` cannot be set from untrusted input.
(2) That `ClusterSetupLinkExchange.Responder` with the new `policy` argument still enforces the pairing-authenticated peer checks.
(3) That the unseen ClusterService.swift hunks do not widen the `responder` property (now non-private) beyond module-internal use.
No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
